solution: For the implication to be false: antecedent T and consequent F. \((p\leftrightarrow\sim q)\) is T when p and q differ, \(p=T,q=F\) or \(p=F,q=T\); \((\sim p\wedge q)\) is F when \(p=T\). Checking: \(p=T,q=F\) gives antecedent T, consequent F. Matches option C.
note: said p <-> ~q is true when p and q are equal; it is true when they differ. Key C unchanged.
